name: OH-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with PVI of R+21
Incumbent David Taylor running with a large fundraising edge
Prediction markets price Republican win at 98%
No polling or expert ratings to suggest a competitive race
model.rationale: The R+21 district lean, Taylor's incumbency and roughly $1.1 million raised against an unknown-quantity challenger, and markets pricing a Republican win at 98% all point the same direction. No polls or expert ratings give any reason to move off the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: Any credible polling showing the challenger within single digits, or major outside spending against Taylor, would warrant revisiting.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Southwest Ohio's 2nd District is deeply Republican territory, with a partisan lean of about 21 points toward the GOP. First-term incumbent David Taylor is running for reelection and has raised over $1 million, holding a clear financial advantage over Democratic challenger Jennifer Mazzuckelli, whose fundraising is not yet reported.

No public polls or expert race ratings are available for this contest, but prediction markets give Taylor roughly a 98% chance of winning. The forecast expects a comfortable Republican victory on the order of 19 points, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of polling rather than any sign of a genuine contest.
